name: Lion diet
lead: The lion diet is a restrictive elimination diet consisting only of ruminant meat (typically beef), salt and water. It is described as a stricter form of the carnivore diet, which allows animal products such as meat, dairy and eggs. [1]
It gained wider attention after Mikhaila Peterson and her father Jordan Peterson said they followed it, and it later circulated on social media such as TikTok. [1]

Dietetic organisations such as the British Dietetic Association and Dietitians Australia have dismissed the carnivore diet as a fad, and commentators note concerns about nutrient gaps. No clinical trials of the lion diet itself have been found. [1]

paras: The carnivore diet, also called the zero-carb diet, excludes fruits, vegetables, grains, legumes, nuts and seeds. The lion diet narrows it further to beef, salt and water. Paul Saladino's 2024 animal-based diet is a looser variant that permits fruit, honey and raw dairy. [1]

Exclusively animal diets have earlier precedents: Bernard Moncriff published a book on one in 1856, Arnaldo Cantani prescribed animal-based diets to diabetic patients in the 1870s, and James H. Salisbury promoted a meat and hot water diet in the 1880s. In 2018 former orthopaedic surgeon Shawn Baker promoted the carnivore diet on social media, while Jordan and Mikhaila Peterson followed the lion diet, which later became a TikTok fad. [1]

Commentators including neurologist Steven Novella (April 2023) have called the carnivore diet a fad. Reported concerns include raised LDL cholesterol, vitamin deficiencies from excluding plant foods, constipation from low fibre, possible colon cancer and gout risk from high red meat intake, and strain on the kidneys from high protein. [1]

timeline.event: Bernard Moncriff publishes a book on an exclusively animal diet. [1]
Shawn Baker promotes the carnivore diet; the Petersons follow the lion diet. [1]
Paul Saladino popularises a looser animal-based diet. [1]

card.summary: Beef, salt and water only: a carnivore-diet variant with no trials behind it and dietitian warnings about nutrient gaps.
card.note: No clinical studies of the lion diet itself were found.

quick.overview:
The lion diet allows only ruminant meat such as beef, plus salt and water. It is a stricter version of the carnivore diet.

It spread through social media after public figures said they followed it, and is usually discussed as an elimination approach rather than for appearance specifically.
quick.mechanism: Proponents describe it as removing all plant foods and other potential triggers. Researchers have not tested this mechanism in the lion diet.
quick.risks: Dietetic bodies call the carnivore diet a fad and cite raised LDL cholesterol, low fibre and vitamin deficiencies from excluding plant foods. No clinical trials of the lion diet were found.
